chapters.title: How Lonely Sits the City
chapters.html:
Lamentations 1

1How lonely sits the city
that was full of people!
She has become like a widow,
she who was great among the nations;
the princess among the provinces
has been put to forced labor.

2She weeps bitterly in the night,
her tears on her cheeks;
among all her lovers
she has no one to comfort her;
all her friends have betrayed her;
they have become her enemies.

3Judah has gone into exile
after affliction and hard servitude;
she lives among the nations;
she finds no resting place;
all her pursuers have overtaken her
in the narrow places.

4The roads to Zion mourn,
for no one comes to the appointed feasts;
all her gates are desolate;
her priests groan;
her virgins are grieving,
and she herself is bitter.

5Her foes have become the head;
her enemies are at ease,
for the LORD has afflicted her
for the multitude of her transgressions;
her little children have gone into captivity
before the foe.

6From the daughter of Zion
all her splendor has departed.
Her princes have become like stags
that find no pasture;
they have gone on without strength
before the pursuer.

7Jerusalem remembers,
in the days of her affliction and her wandering,
all the precious things
that were hers from days of old.
When her people fell into the hand of the foe,
and there was no one to help her,
the foes saw her
and laughed at her downfall.

8Jerusalem has sinned greatly;
therefore she has become a thing unclean;
all who honored her despise her,
for they have seen her nakedness;
she herself groans
and turns away.

9Her uncleanness was in her skirts;
she did not remember her end;
she has come down astonishingly,
with no one to comfort her.
"See, LORD, my affliction,
for the enemy has made himself great!"

10The foe has spread out his hand
over all her precious things;
for she has seen nations
enter her sanctuary,
those of whom You commanded
that they should not enter Your assembly.

11All her people groan
as they search for bread;
they give their precious things for food
to bring back their life.
"See, LORD, and look,
for I have become worthless."

12Is it nothing to you, all you who pass by?
Look and see
if there is any pain like my pain,
which was dealt to me,
which the LORD inflicted
on the day of His fierce anger.

13From on high He sent fire
into my bones, and it overcame them;
He spread a net for my feet;
He turned me back;
He has made me desolate,
faint all the day long.

14The yoke of my transgressions is bound fast;
by His hand they are knotted together;
they have come up on my neck;
He has made my strength fail;
the Lord has given me into the hands
of those I cannot stand against.

15The Lord has thrown aside
all my mighty men in my midst;
He has called an appointed time against me
to crush my young men;
the Lord has trodden as in a winepress
the virgin daughter of Judah.

16For these things I weep;
my eye, my eye runs down with water;
for a comforter is far from me,
one to bring back my life;
my children are desolate,
for the enemy has prevailed.

17Zion spreads out her hands,
but there is no one to comfort her;
the LORD has commanded against Jacob
that his neighbors should be his foes;
Jerusalem has become
an unclean thing among them.

18The LORD is righteous,
for I have rebelled against His command.
Hear now, all you peoples,
and see my pain;
my virgins and my young men
have gone into captivity.

19I called to my lovers,
but they deceived me;
my priests and my elders
perished in the city,
while they searched for food
to bring back their life.

20See, LORD, how distressed I am;
my insides churn;
my heart is turned over within me,
for I have been very rebellious.
Outside the sword bereaves;
in the house it is like death.

21They have heard how I groan,
with no one to comfort me;
all my enemies have heard of my trouble;
they rejoice that You have done it.
Bring the day You have announced,
and let them be like me.

22Let all their evil come before You;
deal with them
as You have dealt with me
for all my transgressions;
for my groans are many,
and my heart is faint.

Notes

  • vv1–22 "How lonely sits the city" — the twenty-two verses begin with the twenty-two letters of the Hebrew alphabet in order, aleph to tav, a pattern English cannot keep. Eikhah, "How," the first word, is the book's Hebrew name. The Greek opens with a line the Hebrew does not have: And it came to pass, after Israel was taken captive and Jerusalem laid waste, that Jeremiah sat weeping, and lamented this lament over Jerusalem and said, and it heads each verse with the name of its letter.

  • v1 "She has become like a widow" — Jeremiah's last oracle against Babylon promised Israel and Judah have not been widowed by their God (Jeremiah 51:5); here the city sits like a widow, not one.

  • vv2, 9, 16, 17, 21 "no one to comfort her" — ein menachem, five times in the chapter: Zion's cry goes unanswered. Isaiah's answer begins with the same word, Comfort, comfort My people (Isaiah 40:1).

  • vv3, 5 "she finds no resting place… Her foes have become the head" — the curses of the law come true: Among those nations you will find no ease, and there will be no resting place for the sole of your foot (Deuteronomy 28:65), and He will be the head, and you will be the tail (28:44). No resting place was the dove's before the waters went down (Genesis 8:9).

  • vv4, 15 "no one comes to the appointed feasts… He has called an appointed time against me" — mo'ed, the appointed feast. The feasts of Zion are empty, and the LORD sets His own appointed time: the day He crushes her young men.

  • v8 "she has become a thing unclean" — nidah, spelled with a yod, is found only here. In v17 Jerusalem becomes niddah, the word for a woman's impurity, and the Greek has that there; here the Greek has a thing tossed about, from nud, "shake, wander," the verb of the head shaken in scorn (Jeremiah 18:16).

  • v10 "nations enter her sanctuary… that they should not enter Your assembly" — the law, No Ammonite or Moabite shall enter the assembly of the LORD (Deuteronomy 23:3): those not allowed into the assembly have walked into the holy place.

  • v12 "Is it nothing to you, all you who pass by?" — lo aleikhem, "not to you," two words that open the verse without a verb: Is it nothing to you? or May it not come to you. The Greek has All you who pass by the way, turn and see.

  • v18 "The LORD is righteous, for I have rebelled" — tsaddiq, the word of Jeremiah's own complaint, You are righteous, LORD (Jeremiah 12:1). The city does not argue: the fault is hers.

chapters.title: The Lord Has Become Like an Enemy
chapters.html:
Lamentations 2

1How the Lord in His anger
has covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud!
He has thrown down from heaven to earth
the splendor of Israel;
He has not remembered His footstool
in the day of His anger.

2The Lord has swallowed up without pity
all the dwellings of Jacob;
in His wrath He has torn down
the strongholds of the daughter of Judah;
He has brought them down to the ground;
He has profaned the kingdom and its princes.

3In fierce anger He has cut off
every horn of Israel;
He has drawn back His right hand
from before the enemy;
He has burned in Jacob like a flaming fire
that devours all around.

4He has bent His bow like an enemy,
with His right hand set like a foe;
He has killed all who were pleasing to the eye;
in the tent of the daughter of Zion
He has poured out His wrath like fire.

5The Lord has become like an enemy;
He has swallowed up Israel;
He has swallowed up all its palaces,
destroyed its strongholds,
and multiplied in the daughter of Judah
mourning and moaning.

6He has stripped His booth like a garden;
He has destroyed His meeting place;
the LORD has made Zion forget
appointed feast and sabbath,
and in His fierce indignation has spurned
king and priest.

7The Lord has rejected His altar,
disowned His sanctuary;
He has given into the hand of the enemy
the walls of her palaces;
they raised a shout in the house of the LORD
as on the day of an appointed feast.

8The LORD determined to destroy
the wall of the daughter of Zion;
He stretched out the measuring line;
He did not hold back His hand from swallowing;
He made rampart and wall lament;
they languish together.

9Her gates have sunk into the ground;
He has ruined and broken her bars;
her king and her princes are among the nations;
the law is no more,
and her prophets too find no vision
from the LORD.

10The elders of the daughter of Zion
sit on the ground in silence;
they have thrown dust on their heads
and put on sackcloth;
the virgins of Jerusalem
have bowed their heads to the ground.

11My eyes are spent with tears;
my insides churn;
my liver is poured out on the ground
because of the ruin of the daughter of my people,
because children and infants faint
in the streets of the city.

12They say to their mothers,
"Where is the grain and the wine?"
as they faint like the wounded
in the streets of the city,
as their life is poured out
on their mothers' bosom.

13What can I say for you?
To what can I compare you,
daughter of Jerusalem?
What can I liken to you, that I may comfort you,
virgin daughter of Zion?
For your ruin is vast as the sea;
who can heal you?

14Your prophets have seen for you
false and foolish visions;
they have not exposed your iniquity
to restore your fortunes,
but have seen for you burdens
false and misleading.

15All who pass along the way
clap their hands at you;
they hiss and shake their heads
at the daughter of Jerusalem:
"Is this the city that was called
the perfection of beauty,
the joy of all the earth?"

16All your enemies
open their mouths against you;
they hiss and gnash their teeth;
they say, "We have swallowed her!
This is the day we waited for;
we have found it; we have seen it!"

17The LORD has done what He purposed;
He has carried out His word,
which He commanded long ago;
He has torn down without pity;
He has made the enemy rejoice over you;
He has raised the horn of your foes.

18Their heart cried out to the Lord.
Wall of the daughter of Zion,
let tears run down like a torrent
day and night!
Give yourself no rest;
let your eyes not be still!

19Arise, cry out in the night,
at the beginning of the watches!
Pour out your heart like water
in the presence of the Lord!
Lift up your hands to Him
for the life of your little children,
who faint from hunger
at the head of every street.

20See, LORD, and look:
to whom have You done this?
Should women eat their own fruit,
the children they have cherished?
Should priest and prophet be killed
in the sanctuary of the Lord?

21Young and old lie on the ground
in the streets;
my virgins and my young men
have fallen by the sword;
You have killed them in the day of Your anger;
You have slaughtered without pity.

22You summoned, as for the day of an appointed feast,
my terrors on every side;
and on the day of the LORD's anger
no one escaped or survived;
those I cherished and reared
my enemy has destroyed.

Notes

  • vv1–22 — another alphabet in order, but here pe comes before ayin (vv16–17), the reverse of chapter 1; chapters 3 and 4 have the same order as this one.

  • v1 "He has covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud… He has not remembered His footstool" — ya'iv, "cloud over," is found only here; the Greek has darkened. His footstool is the ark, David's house of rest for the ark of the covenant of the LORD and for the footstool of our God (1 Chronicles 28:2), and the temple where Israel would worship at His footstool (Psalm 132:7).

  • vv2, 5, 8, 16 "The Lord has swallowed up… He has swallowed up Israel… from swallowing… We have swallowed her!" — bala, four times. Three times the Lord swallows; the fourth time the enemies boast of it as their own work.

  • vv6–7, 22 "His meeting place… appointed feast and sabbath… as on the day of an appointed feast… as for the day of an appointed feast" — mo'ed, the word of the tent of meeting and of the feasts, as in 1:4, 15. The shouting in the temple now is the enemy's, and the feast the LORD calls is a day of terror.

  • v8 "He stretched out the measuring line" — the builder's line used to pull down, as the LORD said through the prophets under Manasseh, I will stretch over Jerusalem the measuring line of Samaria (2 Kings 21:13).

  • v11 "my liver is poured out on the ground" — kaved, "liver," an inward part like me'ai, "my insides," in the same verse: the grief is in the body. The Greek reads kavod, "my glory," from the same letters.

  • v14 "burdens false and misleading" — masa'ot, the prophets' word burden for an oracle, which Jeremiah turned against them: You are the burden (Jeremiah 23:33).

  • v15 "the perfection of beauty, the joy of all the earth" — the psalms' names for Zion, the joy of all the earth (Psalm 48:2) and the perfection of beauty (Psalm 50:2), now in the mouths of those who mock her.

  • v20 "Should women eat their own fruit?" — the last curse of the siege in the law, You will eat the fruit of your womb (Deuteronomy 28:53).

  • v22 "my terrors on every side" — megurai missaviv, Jeremiah's cry terror on every side (Jeremiah 6:25; 20:3), now in Zion's own mouth.

chapters.title: New Every Morning
chapters.html:
Lamentations 3

1I am the man who has seen affliction
by the rod of His wrath.

2It is I He has led and made to walk
in darkness and not light.

3Against me alone He turns His hand
again and again, all the day.

4He has worn out my flesh and my skin;
He has broken my bones.

5He has built up against me and surrounded me
with poison and hardship.

6He has made me dwell in darkness
like those long dead.

7He has walled me in so that I cannot go out;
He has made my chains heavy.

8Though I cry out and call for help,
He shuts out my prayer.

9He has walled up my ways with hewn stone;
He has made my paths crooked.

10He is to me a bear lying in wait,
a lion in hiding;

11He turned aside my ways and tore me to pieces;
He has made me desolate.

12He bent His bow
and set me up as a target for the arrow.

13He drove into my kidneys
the arrows of His quiver.

14I have become the laughingstock of all my people,
their mocking song all the day.

15He has filled me with bitter herbs;
He has made me drink my fill of wormwood.

16He has broken my teeth on gravel;
He has made me cower in ashes.

17My soul is cast off from peace;
I have forgotten what good is.

18So I said, "My strength has perished,
and my hope from the LORD."

19Remember my affliction and my wandering,
the wormwood and the poison!

20My soul surely remembers
and is bowed down within me.

21This I call to mind;
therefore I have hope:

22It is the LORD's loyal love that we are not finished,
for His compassions do not fail;

23they are new every morning;
great is Your faithfulness.

24"The LORD is my portion," says my soul;
"therefore I will hope in Him."

25The LORD is good to those who wait for Him,
to the soul who seeks Him.

26It is good to hope and wait in silence
for the salvation of the LORD.

27It is good for a man
to bear the yoke in his youth.

28Let him sit alone and be silent,
when He has laid it on him;

29let him put his mouth in the dust —
perhaps there may be hope;

30let him give his cheek to the one who strikes him,
and be filled with reproach.

31For the Lord
will not cast off forever.

32Though He causes grief, He will have compassion
according to the abundance of His loyal love;

33for He does not afflict from His heart
or grieve the children of men.

34To crush underfoot
all the prisoners of the earth,

35to turn aside a man's right
in the presence of the Most High,

36to wrong a man in his cause —
the Lord does not approve.

37Who has spoken and it came to be,
unless the Lord has commanded it?

38Is it not from the mouth of the Most High
that evil and good go forth?

39Why should a living man complain,
a man, about his sins?

40Let us search out and examine our ways,
and return to the LORD.

41Let us lift up our hearts with our hands
to God in heaven:

42"We have transgressed and rebelled,
and You have not forgiven.

43You have wrapped Yourself in anger and pursued us;
You have killed without pity.

44You have wrapped Yourself in a cloud,
so that no prayer can pass through.

45You have made us scum and refuse
among the peoples.

46All our enemies
have opened their mouths against us;

47terror and the pit have come upon us,
devastation and ruin."

48My eye runs down with streams of water
because of the ruin of the daughter of my people.

49My eye flows and does not cease,
without respite,

50until the LORD looks down
and sees from heaven;

51my eye brings grief to my soul
because of all the daughters of my city.

52Those who are my enemies without cause
have hunted me down like a bird;

53they have ended my life in the pit
and thrown stones on me;

54water flowed over my head;
I said, "I am cut off."

55I called on Your name, LORD,
from the lowest pit;

56You heard my voice: "Do not close Your ear
to my sighing, to my cry for help!"

57You came near on the day I called to You;
You said, "Do not fear!"

58You have pleaded my cause, Lord;
You have redeemed my life.

59You have seen, LORD, the wrong done to me;
judge my case.

60You have seen all their vengeance,
all their plans against me.

61You have heard their reproach, LORD,
all their plans against me,

62the lips of my assailants and their muttering
against me all the day.

63Look at their sitting and their rising;
I am their mocking song.

64You will repay them, LORD,
according to the work of their hands.

65You will give them a veiled heart;
Your curse be on them!

66You will pursue them in anger and destroy them
from under the heavens of the LORD.

Notes

  • vv1–66 "I am the man who has seen affliction" — the alphabet again, but each letter now begins three verses in a row: three aleph, three bet, and so on, sixty-six verses. The speaker is one man, ha-gever, "the man," and the chapter moves from his own suffering (vv1–20) to hope (vv21–39), to the people's prayer (vv40–47) and back to him (vv48–66).

  • vv7–15 "He has walled me in… He has walled up my ways… He set me up as a target… wormwood" — the words of Job's complaints, He has walled up my way, so that I cannot pass (Job 19:8) and He set me up as His target (Job 16:12), and of Jeremiah's sentence on the people, I am about to feed this people with wormwood (Jeremiah 9:15). He has made me dwell in darkness like those long dead (v6) is word for word in Psalm 143:3.

  • vv19–24 "Remember my affliction and my wandering… This I call to mind; therefore I have hope… The LORD is my portion" — affliction and wandering are the words of Jerusalem's memory in 1:7; here, remembering them, the man turns. The LORD is my portion is the psalm's word (Psalm 119:57) and the Levites' inheritance, I am your share and your inheritance (Numbers 18:20). The Greek has nothing of vv22–24.

  • v22 "It is the LORD's loyal love that we are not finished" — ki lo tamnu, "that we are not finished," as the Hebrew is pointed; the same letters read tammu would make it The LORD's loyal love does not cease, matching the next line, His compassions do not fail.

  • v30 "let him give his cheek to the one who strikes him" — the servant of Isaiah, I gave… my cheeks to those who pull out the beard (Isaiah 50:6), and Jesus' word, If anyone strikes you on the right cheek, turn to him the other also (Matthew 5:39).

  • v36 "to wrong a man in his cause — the Lord does not approve" — Adonai lo ra'ah, "the Lord does not see," which can be a statement, does not approve (he does not look on it with favor), or a question, Does the Lord not see?

  • v38 "Is it not from the mouth of the Most High that evil and good go forth?" — Job's answer to his wife, Shall we receive good from God, and not receive evil? (Job 2:10), and the LORD's word in Isaiah, I make peace and create disaster (Isaiah 45:7).

  • vv43–44, 8 "You have wrapped Yourself in a cloud, so that no prayer can pass through" — the cloud of 2:1, now a wall against prayer, as at v8, He shuts out my prayer.

  • vv52–58 "they have ended my life in the pit and thrown stones on me… I called on Your name, LORD, from the lowest pit… You said, 'Do not fear!'" — bor, the word of Jeremiah's cistern (Jeremiah 38:6), though there There was no water in the cistern, only mud. The lowest pit is the psalm's, You have put me in the lowest pit (Psalm 88:6), and Do not fear is what Jeremiah heard at his call, Do not be afraid of them (Jeremiah 1:8). You have redeemed my life: ga'al, the redeemer's verb (Jeremiah 50:34).

He has built up against me and surrounded me with poison and hardship.
He has made me dwell in darkness like those long dead.
He has walled me in so that I cannot go out; He has made my chains heavy.
Though I cry out and call for help, He shuts out my prayer.
He has walled up my ways with hewn stone; He has made my paths crooked.
He is to me a bear lying in wait, a lion in hiding;
He turned aside my ways and tore me to pieces; He has made me desolate.
He bent His bow and set me up as a target for the arrow.
He drove into my kidneys the arrows of His quiver.
I have become the laughingstock of all my people, their mocking song all the day.
He has filled me with bitter herbs; He has made me drink my fill of wormwood.
He has broken my teeth on gravel; He has made me cower in ashes.
My soul is cast off from peace; I have forgotten what good is.
So I said, "My strength has perished, and my hope from the LORD."
Remember my affliction and my wandering, the wormwood and the poison!
My soul surely remembers and is bowed down within me.
This I call to mind; therefore I have hope:
It is the LORD's loyal love that we are not finished, for His compassions do not fail;
they are new every morning; great is Your faithfulness.
"The LORD is my portion," says my soul; "therefore I will hope in Him."
The LORD is good to those who wait for Him, to the soul who seeks Him.
It is good to hope and wait in silence for the salvation of the LORD.
It is good for a man to bear the yoke in his youth.
Let him sit alone and be silent, when He has laid it on him;
let him put his mouth in the dust — perhaps there may be hope;
let him give his cheek to the one who strikes him, and be filled with reproach.
For the Lord will not cast off forever.
Though He causes grief, He will have compassion according to the abundance of His loyal love;
for He does not afflict from His heart or grieve the children of men.
To crush underfoot all the prisoners of the earth,
to turn aside a man's right in the presence of the Most High,
to wrong a man in his cause — the Lord does not approve.
Who has spoken and it came to be, unless the Lord has commanded it?
Is it not from the mouth of the Most High that evil and good go forth?
Why should a living man complain, a man, about his sins?
Let us search out and examine our ways, and return to the LORD.
Let us lift up our hearts with our hands to God in heaven:
"We have transgressed and rebelled, and You have not forgiven.
You have wrapped Yourself in anger and pursued us; You have killed without pity.
You have wrapped Yourself in a cloud, so that no prayer can pass through.
You have made us scum and refuse among the peoples.
All our enemies have opened their mouths against us;
terror and the pit have come upon us, devastation and ruin."
My eye runs down with streams of water because of the ruin of the daughter of my people.
My eye flows and does not cease, without respite,
until the LORD looks down and sees from heaven;
my eye brings grief to my soul because of all the daughters of my city.
Those who are my enemies without cause have hunted me down like a bird;
they have ended my life in the pit and thrown stones on me;
water flowed over my head; I said, "I am cut off."
I called on Your name, LORD, from the lowest pit;
You heard my voice: "Do not close Your ear to my sighing, to my cry for help!"
You came near on the day I called to You; You said, "Do not fear!"
You have pleaded my cause, Lord; You have redeemed my life.
You have seen, LORD, the wrong done to me; judge my case.
You have seen all their vengeance, all their plans against me.
You have heard their reproach, LORD, all their plans against me,
the lips of my assailants and their muttering against me all the day.
Look at their sitting and their rising; I am their mocking song.
You will repay them, LORD, according to the work of their hands.
You will give them a veiled heart; Your curse be on them!
You will pursue them in anger and destroy them from under the heavens of the LORD.

chapters.title: How the Gold Has Grown Dim
chapters.html:
Lamentations 4

1How the gold has grown dim,
the fine gold changed!
The holy stones lie scattered
at the head of every street.

2The precious sons of Zion,
worth their weight in fine gold,
how they are counted as clay jars,
the work of a potter's hands!

3Even jackals offer the breast
and nurse their young,
but the daughter of my people has become cruel,
like the ostriches in the wilderness.

4The tongue of the nursing infant
sticks to the roof of its mouth for thirst;
the children beg for bread,
but no one breaks it for them.

5Those who ate delicacies
lie desolate in the streets;
those brought up in scarlet
cling to heaps of refuse.

6The iniquity of the daughter of my people
is greater than the sin of Sodom,
which was overthrown in a moment,
and no hands were laid on her.

7Her consecrated ones were purer than snow,
whiter than milk;
their bodies were more ruddy than coral,
their form like sapphire.

8Now their faces are blacker than soot;
they are not recognized in the streets;
their skin has shriveled on their bones;
it has become dry as wood.

9Those slain by the sword were better off
than those slain by hunger,
who waste away, pierced through
for lack of the fruits of the field.

10The hands of compassionate women
have boiled their own children;
they became their food
in the ruin of the daughter of my people.

11The LORD has spent His wrath;
He has poured out His fierce anger;
He has kindled a fire in Zion
that has devoured its foundations.

12The kings of the earth did not believe,
nor any of the inhabitants of the world,
that foe or enemy could enter
the gates of Jerusalem.

13It was for the sins of her prophets
and the iniquities of her priests,
who shed in her midst
the blood of the righteous.

14They wandered blind through the streets,
so defiled with blood
that no one was able
to touch their garments.

15"Away! Unclean!" people cried at them.
"Away! Away! Do not touch!"
So they fled and wandered;
it was said among the nations,
"They shall stay here as guests no longer."

16The face of the LORD has scattered them;
He will look on them no more;
they showed no regard for the priests,
no favor to the elders.

17Our eyes still fail,
looking in vain for help;
from our watchtower we watched
for a nation that could not save.

18They hunted our steps,
so that we could not walk in our streets;
our end drew near; our days were fulfilled,
for our end had come.

19Our pursuers were swifter
than the eagles of the heavens;
they chased us on the mountains;
they lay in wait for us in the wilderness.

20The breath of our nostrils, the LORD's anointed,
was caught in their pits,
he of whom we said, "Under his shadow
we shall live among the nations."

21Rejoice and be glad, daughter of Edom,
you who live in the land of Uz!
To you also the cup will pass;
you will be drunk and strip yourself bare.

22Your iniquity is ended, daughter of Zion;
He will not carry you into exile again;
He will punish your iniquity, daughter of Edom;
He will uncover your sins.

Notes

  • vv1–22 — the alphabet once more, one verse to a letter, with pe before ayin as in chapter 2. The verses are shorter, two lines of Hebrew each.

  • v2 "counted as clay jars, the work of a potter's hands" — the picture of the potter in Jeremiah: the clay in the potter's hand (Jeremiah 18:4–6), the potter's flask broken in the valley (19:1, 10–11). The sons of Zion, weighed against gold, are valued now like cheap earthenware.

  • v3 "like the ostriches in the wilderness" — the bird of Job's poem, who treats her young harshly, as if they were not hers (Job 39:16). The jackal suckles its young; the mothers of Jerusalem cannot.

  • vv6, 9–10 "greater than the sin of Sodom, which was overthrown in a moment… The hands of compassionate women have boiled their own children" — Sodom's end was quick; Jerusalem's was a long siege. The law's curse, the woman most tender and delicate among you who will eat them secretly for lack of everything (Deuteronomy 28:56–57), and the famine of Samaria, So we boiled my son and ate him (2 Kings 6:29), have come again.

  • v7 "Her consecrated ones were purer than snow" — nezireha, "her ones set apart": the word of the Nazirite's vow, and of Joseph, the one set apart from his brothers (Genesis 49:26). It can mean her princes or her Nazirites; the Greek has her Nazirites.

  • vv13–16 "for the sins of her prophets and the iniquities of her priests… 'Away! Unclean!'" — the priests and prophets who demanded Jeremiah's death (Jeremiah 26:8) now walk the streets with blood on them, shouted at as the law made the one with blight cry out, "Unclean! Unclean!" (Leviticus 13:45). Lagur, "stay as guests": even as guests among the nations they are not wanted.

  • v20 "The breath of our nostrils, the LORD's anointed, was caught in their pits" — Zedekiah, caught in the plains of Jericho as he fled (Jeremiah 39:5; 52:8). Under his shadow we shall live among the nations was the hope that went with him.

  • vv21–22 "daughter of Edom, you who live in the land of Uz! To you also the cup will pass… Your iniquity is ended, daughter of Zion" — Uz and Edom drink from the cup of Jeremiah 25:20–21, all the kings of the land of Uz… Edom; Uz is Job's land (Job 1:1). The chapter ends with Zion's punishment finished and Edom's begun.

chapters.title: Remember, LORD
chapters.html:
Lamentations 5

1Remember, LORD, what has happened to us;
look, and see our disgrace!

2Our inheritance has been turned over to strangers,
our houses to foreigners.

3We have become orphans, fatherless;
our mothers are like widows.

4We must pay money for the water we drink;
our wood comes to us for a price.

5With a yoke on our necks we are driven;
we are weary and given no rest.

6We have given our hand to Egypt,
and to Assyria, to get enough bread.

7Our fathers sinned, and are no more,
and we bear their iniquities.

8Slaves rule over us;
there is no one to rescue us from their hand.

9We get our bread at the risk of our lives,
because of the sword in the wilderness.

10Our skin is hot as an oven
from the burning heat of famine.

11Women are raped in Zion,
virgins in the cities of Judah.

12Princes are hanged by their hands;
no respect is shown to the elders.

13Young men carry the millstones,
and boys stagger under loads of wood.

14The elders have left the gate,
the young men their music.

15The joy of our hearts has ceased;
our dancing has turned to mourning.

16The crown has fallen from our head;
woe to us, for we have sinned!

17For this our heart has grown faint;
for these things our eyes have grown dim,

18for Mount Zion, which lies desolate,
with foxes prowling over it.

19You, LORD, are enthroned forever;
Your throne is to all generations.

20Why do You forget us forever,
forsake us for so many days?

21Bring us back to You, LORD, that we may return;
renew our days as of old,

22unless You have utterly rejected us,
and are very angry with us.

Notes

  • vv1–22 "Remember, LORD, what has happened to us" — twenty-two verses, the number of the alphabet, but no longer in its order: the acrostic has broken off. The voice is we throughout, a prayer of the people.

  • v6 "We have given our hand to Egypt, and to Assyria" — the policy Jeremiah mocked at the start, what are you doing on the road to Egypt… on the road to Assyria? (Jeremiah 2:18). Given the hand is a pledge of submission.

  • v7 "Our fathers sinned, and are no more, and we bear their iniquities" — the proverb Jeremiah said would one day end, The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge (Jeremiah 31:29); v16 adds for we have sinned.

  • vv16, 18 "The crown has fallen from our head… Mount Zion, which lies desolate, with foxes prowling over it" — Jeremiah's word to the king and the queen mother, your beautiful crown has come down from your heads (Jeremiah 13:18), and Micah's, quoted at Jeremiah's trial, Zion shall be plowed as a field (Jeremiah 26:18).

  • v19 "You, LORD, are enthroned forever" — the line of the psalm, But You, LORD, are enthroned forever (Psalm 102:12): the city's throne is gone; His is not.

  • v21 "Bring us back to You, LORD, that we may return" — the words of Ephraim's repentance in Jeremiah, Bring me back, that I may return (Jeremiah 31:18).

  • v22 "unless You have utterly rejected us, and are very angry with us" — ki im, which can mean unless, but, or even though, and the book ends on it without an answer. Read as unless, the last verse names the one fear that could undo the prayer of v21; read as but, it is a statement, But You have utterly rejected us; the Greek has For You have utterly rejected us.
